A privilege escalation vulnerability has been discovered in a MSI package that spawns `cmd.exe` process in an interactive and unsandboxed context. These processes are briefly visible in the user's desktop session, allowing an attacker with limited privileges to hijack the execution context and elevate privileges on the system.

### Details
A privilege escalation vulnerability exists in the repair functionality of Netbird MSI installer, where `cmd.exe` and is spawned in the context of the user’s interactive session. During repair operations, the MSI uses custom actions in an insecure manner. A local, low-privileged attacker can exploit these custom actions by invoking the cached MSI file to execute arbitrary code. This results in privilege escalation, granting a command prompt in the context of NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM.

### PoC
1. Find the MSI
     - Locate the cached MSI under C:\Windows\Installer. Use timestamps or Mandiant’s helper script:
        [msi_search.ps1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mandiant/msi-search/main/msi_search.ps1)

2. Run Repair
     - Trigger repair using:

    `msiexec.exe /fa C:\Windows\Installer\<target>.msi`

3. Pause a Spawned Window
     - When a command window appear, quickly select text to pause.

4. Elevate to SYSTEM
     - Right-click title bar → Properties → Enable Legacy Console
     - Use Link to open default browser (e.g., Firefox)
     - Press Ctrl+O, type cmd, hit Enter → A SYSTEM command prompt is launched.

![netbird_msi_priv](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/06c45a3b-9f98-4b07-8908-d57ffb8527e0)
![netbird_properties](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c557292c-a740-4977-9b5c-09db78ec17c9)
![netbird_cmd](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dd0cb5d8-c197-432b-b179-dc4f0d952635)

### Impact
Successful exploitation allows a local attacker to escalate privileges to SYSTEM, potentially leading to full compromise of the affected system.

### Affected platforms
Windows only. The affected custom actions live in the MSI installer, which first shipped in v0.23.0. Packaging on other platforms does not use them.

### Fix
Fixed in 0.49.0 ([#4041](https://github.com/netbirdio/netbird/pull/4041)). The MSI no longer launches a command interpreter during any custom action: the `cmd` property and the two `taskkill` actions that ran through it were removed from the WiX definition. A repair operation therefore spawns no interactive console for a low-privileged user to take over.

The current installer defines a single custom action, which runs a bundled binary silently from the MSI Binary table rather than through a shell.
